Application Materials.content:
Applications will not be considered until all required documents have been uploaded.
- **Degree certificate(s) and academic transcripts: Required.** From first and subsequent degrees. Degree certificates and transcripts should comply with standard requirements outlined on the guidance pages.
- **Personal statement: Optional.** Personal statements are not required for this programme as they do not form part of the routine application assessment process. However, where an applicant is slightly below the typical entry requirements, the personal statement, if provided, may be used to look for additional context and detail about relevant work experience and achievements. Applicants are welcome to submit a personal statement as an additional document to support their application if they wish to do so. Non-standard applicants should use the personal statement to provide further details.
- **English language certificates/other evidence: Required.** Evidence of meeting the English language profile as stated on the Postgraduate Prospectus and specified by the University English Language Requirements Policy.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV): Optional.** CVs might include details of other relevant work experience and qualifications to support an application.
- Applicants whose education has been significantly disrupted through health or personal problems, disability or specific difficulties within their studies can submit an **extenuating circumstances form** as part of the application.

Interview Requirements.content: Interviews do not form part of the admissions process.

Application Deadlines.content:
Start date: **September 2026**.
Application deadline: Overseas applicants: **13 August 2026**. Home applicants: **10 September 2026**.
Please note that due to high demand, some programmes may close earlier than advertised. Early applications are advised to avoid disappointment. Places are limited and allocated on a continuous basis from **September 2025** until all places are filled.

Academic Requirements.content:
- You will typically need **an upper second-class honours degree or an international equivalent in a quantitative subject** (whether as a single, joint or combined honours degree) such as Accounting and Finance, Actuarial Sciences, Computer Science, Data Science, Economics, Engineering, Finance, International Economics and Trade, Mathematics, Physics, Commerce (with specialism in Accounting/Finance/Economics).
- If your degree is not listed above, you need **a 2:1 or equivalent in two different quantitative units** from the [Maths qualification requirements](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/taught/msc-business-analytics/#accordion-163258) list.
- Alternatively, you need **A-level Mathematics with grade A** if there are no mathematics or quantitative units in your degree.
- If your degree subject is not listed in the main entry requirements, you must have evidence of **an upper second class honours degree which includes two units of mathematics with 60% or above (or international equivalent) in each unit**. Examples of acceptable units include Advanced Maths, Algebra/Linear Algebra, Calculus, Financial Maths, Maths, Pure Maths, Business Mathematics, Business Statistics, Computer Science (including programming/algorithms), Data Mining/Data Science/Data Analytics, Derivatives, Econometrics, Financial Modelling, Financial Statement Analysis, Investment Analysis, Probability, Quantitative Methods, Quantitative Research Methods, and Statistics/Statistical Methods/Statistical Analysis.
- We will consider your application if your interim grades are currently slightly lower than the programme's entry requirements and may make you an aspirational offer; you would need to achieve the standard entry requirements by the end of your degree, and specific module requirements would still apply.
- If your achieved grade is lower than the entry requirements, your application may be more likely to receive an offer if you have additional relevant work experience or qualifications, including **relevant work experience (5 years minimum)** in Digital Marketing, Data/Business Analytics, Data Science, Data Engineering, Banking and Finance, or other sectors requiring expertise in business/data analytics/analysis and/or statistics, or **a relevant postgraduate qualification**.
- China-specific: To be considered for admission to a master's degree programme at the University of Bristol, the minimum requirement is typically an undergraduate degree from an acceptable institution equivalent to a UK upper second-class degree (2:1). Applicants who hold **a four-year bachelor's (honours) degree from an accepted Chinese university with a minimum of 78% - 87%** will be considered; the required percentage depends on the undergraduate university and the programme applied for. Qualifications from selected institutions may require accreditation.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
For Profile B, postgraduate programmes require the listed English language level. Accepted tests are valid when taken **no more than two years before the start date** of the programme; component scores must be met fully through **one sitting** of the test and scores cannot be combined from multiple certificates.
- IELTS Academic / IELTS Academic for UKVI: **PG: 7.0 overall with 6.5 in all skills**.
- TOEFL iBT and TOEFL at Home: for tests taken up to **20 January 2026**, **PG: 95 overall with R22, L21, S23, W22**; for tests taken from **21 January 2026 onwards**, **PG: 5 overall with 4.5 in all skills**.
- Pearson PTE Academic / Pearson PTE Academic UKVI: **PG: 71 overall with no lower than 67 in all skills**.
- C1 Advanced (CAE): **PG: Grade C, or Level B2 with 176 in all skills**.
- C2 Proficiency (CPE): **Grade C, or Level C1 with 184 in writing and 176 in all other skills**.
- Trinity Integrated Skills in English (ISE): **PG: Level III or IV test with 105 overall and 96 in all skills**.
- LanguageCert Academic / LanguageCert Academic SELT: **PG: C1 level with 75 overall and 70 in all skills**.
- Skills for English: **C1 Pass or C2 Pass**.
- Other accepted English Language Proficiency Tests include NCUK EAP; University of Portsmouth Pre-Sessional English; Heriot-Watt Pre-Sessional English; Strathclyde ELT; Kaplan EAP; Oxford International ELLT; University of Warwick EAP; and AEMG Direct Entry Programme EAP, with the listed Profile B grades.
Applicants who are nationals of listed English-speaking countries will generally be exempt from providing additional evidence of English language ability. Applicants who have studied one of the listed qualifications in an English-speaking country may meet the University's English language requirements: final four years of high school education; two years of a full-time Bachelor's degree; one year of a Master's degree; or two years of a TNE/international partnership degree. In all cases, **the qualification must have been awarded no more than seven years prior to the start of the degree programme**.
Applicants with a university-level qualification listed above, when fully taught and examined in English, may also meet the University's English language requirements with an official Medium of Instruction (MOI) letter confirming that English is the medium of teaching and examination, or an ECCTIS English Language Proficiency Statement confirming the degree is comparable to an English language level of C1 or above.
Applicants can demonstrate ongoing engagement with English post-study through work experience in a listed English-speaking country if they have worked for **a minimum of two years** where the main language for the role was English, the role involved daily professional use of English, and the role ended **no more than two years before** the course start date. The University reserves the right to refuse an English language exemption if it has concerns about an applicant's abilities.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc Business Analytics is a professionally accredited, one-year specialist programme for students aiming to master the latest techniques in descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. Students develop skills to integrate advanced data analytics with business decision-making, bridge the gap between technical expertise and business leadership, and collaborate effectively with decision-makers in diverse organisational contexts.
Accredited by the [Institute of Analytics (IoA)](https://ioaglobal.org/), MSc Business Analytics emphasises professional and ethical standards while enhancing employability. Designed with industry insights from leading organisations such as IBM, NHS, Amazon, and Barilla Group, and enriched by alumni feedback, it delivers a cutting-edge education.
The programme offers opportunities to work with the Professional Liaison Network (PLN) on consulting projects, providing hands-on experience with organisations. Students work on real-world challenges with partners like Barilla, Yeo Valley, Financial Times, IBM, and Bristol Airport, covering topics such as resource allocation, people analytics, customer segmentation, performance measurement, healthcare workforce analysis, and renewable energy systems automation.
Students gain experience with decision-support tools such as:
- Python
- R
- MS Excel
- Tableau for data visualisation
- Lingo for ad-hoc analytics
Alumni and industry panel discussions, guest lectures by business analytics experts from a variety of sectors, career development workshops, technology sessions on industry tools such as PowerBI, SQL, and @RISK, and mentorship programmes connecting students with alumni and industry experts are integral elements.
The programme covers:
- Mastering data identification, extraction, and cleaning techniques to ensure high-quality datasets.
- Applying statistical and machine learning methods for data mining and predictive analytics.
- Formulating and executing statistical and mathematical models to drive optimal business decisions.
- Visualising, interpreting, and communicating the results of statistical analyses to inform decision-making.
The programme is taught at the Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus, with enhanced links with businesses providing real-world knowledge, networks and skills, and students also benefit from access to student services and facilities at the Clifton Campus.
Key information: Programme duration is one year full-time; delivery method is on-campus; location is [Temple Quarter](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/temple-quarter-enterprise-campus/) as the main location and [Clifton campus](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/clifton-campus/); award available is MSc.
Successful completion of four core units, two optional units, and a final business analytics dissertation project lead to an MSc Business Analytics award. In the first term, core units provide a foundation in descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. In the second term, students can choose electives to deepen expertise. Students attend the mandatory Business Analytics Consulting Project unit, applying knowledge to real-life business problems for an external client. In the summer term, students undertake the Business Analytics Dissertation Project, applying acquired knowledge to research a topic of interest, enhancing critical analysis skills, exploring real-world business problems, providing practical solutions, and communicating findings to relevant stakeholders.
The MSc Business Analytics programme addresses the growing demand for business analytics expertise in the UK and globally. Graduates have secured roles at leading organizations including PwC China, Capgemini, Deloitte South Asia, Reckitt, Volkswagen, EDF Trading, Jaguar Land Rover UK, 3Vision, Low Carbon Contracts Company, Play Sports Network, and MTC - Manufacturing Technology Centre. Graduates pursue careers across industries such as technology, consulting, finance, automotive, manufacturing, and analytical roles. Common career paths include Business Analytics Specialist/Professional, Management Consultant, Product Manager, Market Research Analyst/Digital Marketing Specialist, Operations/Data Analyst, Modelling/Data Scientist, Business Operations Analytics Specialist, HR/People/Insurance Analytics Specialist, and Financial Analyst.

We spoke to a range of undergraduate and postgraduate students in the **2025/26 academic year** to ask them about their cost of living as a student in Bristol. This revealed that the average monthly spend is **£1,862 for postgraduate students**.
A student’s average monthly spend includes:
| Living cost categories | Postgraduate students |

| Rent/Mortgage (monthly) | £871.47 |
| Electricity, gas and water (monthly) | £74.83 |
| Internet, landline & mobile (monthly) | £24.99 |

| Public transport (monthly) | £34.68 |
| Private transport (annual/one-off purchases) | £181.56 |
| Private transport (monthly) | £21.90 |
| Medical expenses (monthly) | £21.83 |
| Laundromats/dry cleaning (monthly) | £3.54 |
| Home entertainment (monthly) | £27.90 |
| Takeaway food (monthly) | £27.46 |

| Nights out (monthly) | £41 |
| Clothes & personal grooming (monthly) | £45.63 |
| Gym, fitness & wellness (monthly) | £28.98 |
Living costs will vary depending on individual circumstances.

Financial Aid.content:
Applications for September 2026 entry are closed. Think Big Scholarship applications closed on **10 April 2026 at 10 am UK time**.
- Think Big international scholarships are for applicants with [overseas fee status](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/fee-status/) who have applied for an eligible undergraduate or master's course.
- Think Big postgraduate scholarships are valued at **£6,500, £13,000 and £26,000** for your first year of study.
- Think Big Postgraduate Scholarships: the awards of **£6,500, £13,000 and £26,000** are available for one year of [any eligible postgraduate master’s programme](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/think-big-scholarships/), including MRes programmes.
- Think Big about Business Postgraduate Scholarships: the awards of **£6,500 and £13,000** are available for international students studying [any eligible postgraduate programme](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/think-big-scholarships/) in the Business School.
- Think Big Career Accelerator: in addition to a place on the programme, the Career Accelerator also includes a **£3,000 scholarship** for international students studying [any eligible postgraduate master’s programme](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/finances/scholarships/think-big-scholarships/), including MRes programmes. This will be applied to the cost of tuition fees.
- Multiple scholarships, one application form: you only need to submit one scholarship application form. Your application will be matched with your University study application and then you will be considered for every scholarship where you meet the necessary eligibility requirements.
- Before starting your scholarship application, you must have applied to study at the University of Bristol and received an application ID.

There is one scholarship of **£13,000** available for a postgraduate international student from each country. This will be applied to the cost of tuition fees.

Multiple Applications.content: You can apply to more than one postgraduate programme at the University. Simply find your programme using the online prospectus and log in to the application system using your existing username and password.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
Offers made may be conditional or unconditional. An unconditional offer will be made to applicants who have already met the conditions and provided evidence that conditions have been met. Where academic or language requirements have not yet been fulfilled, applicants will receive a conditional offer outlining the requirements that must be met.
Applicants who receive a conditional offer will be required to submit all final results to meet their offer conditions by the date noted in their offer letter. Offer holders who are unable to provide their final results by this date should email choosebristol-pg@bristol.ac.uk to notify the team as soon as possible.
